shared_elements: large standing stone monolith carved in shallow low relief
small animal/bird-like figures in profile relief
suggestion of an anthropomorphic body (arms/limbs indicated in flat relief)
justification: Both are monumental slab-like stones whose faces are organised into stacked zones by a horizontal band, with shallow, flat, low-relief motifs including discs, zigzag bands and small creature figures, and both read as loosely anthropomorphic bodies with limbs rendered as relief lines. The decisive difference is the composition: A is a fully modelled figure with a sculpted head, encircling arms and a belt built around a single central disc, whereas B is a plain rectangular pillar carrying multiple small repeated animal-like reliefs in registers with no carved head or bodily volume.
